context.process_name: Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices
context.objective: Document how we carry out Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?

It starts when cash proceeds are received or expected, when a deal closes or a realization happens, or when the client asks us to calculate or carry out a distribution. It is event-driven, there is no fixed calendar for it.

The first step is mine as the event preparer on the capital activity team or the Fund Team. I take the client instructions and the bank records and confirm the entity, the deal, the amount, whether the cash is only expected or has actually been received, and the requested payment date. I work out whether it is a distribution-only event or a combined call-and-distribution event, which we call a net event. Then I assign a second reviewer, list what we will need from the client's tax team, and link the work to the controlling FA-01 event calendar. All of that goes into the event brief and the capital activity workbook.

There is one branch at this point. If the cash has come in and I know which deal it belongs to, I carry on to classifying the proceeds. If cash has come in without deal context, or the client's instructions conflict with each other, I escalate and the client has to identify and classify it in writing before I model anything, and I keep that written confirmation with the bank support.
Once the deal is identified, what do you use to determine how the proceeds are classified?

I use the client's deal information, the bank activity and the closing support. That is the second step, identifying and classifying the proceeds, and I do it as the event preparer.

First I confirm whether the amount is expected cash or cash that has actually cleared the bank. I match the cash to the right portfolio company, deal, fund and bank account. Then I classify each component as return of capital, realized gain, dividend or income, or another supported category, and I flag any asset conversion, escrow, holdback or other piece that changes the distribution economics. It all goes into the proceeds-input tab of the workbook, with the bank support and the client correspondence kept alongside. My check before moving on is that the total classified proceeds equal the amount being modeled and that every component has support behind it.

The branch here is about whether the support is enough. If it is, I move on to updating the cumulative proceeds. If the bank activity on its own does not tell me the deal or the character of the money, I stop the calculations and get a written classification from the client. I never decide the deal, tax or GAAP classification from the bank description alone.
How do you update the cumulative proceeds after the classified proceeds pass your check?

I start with the prior approved cumulative proceeds working file and add the current proceeds to it by their supported classification. Then I confirm the prior distributions, the remaining invested capital and the cumulative contributions.

After that I reconcile the starting balance and the current balance to the prior event, the general ledger, the trial balance, the bank records and the partner-capital records. For the historical balances I pull the system power report, the trial balance and the partner-capital files. I do the work as the preparer and the second reviewer verifies it.

The branch is on the reconciliation. If every difference is resolved or documented, I have a reconciled waterfall starting point and I go on to confirming the waterfall rules for the fund. If the starting point has a difference I cannot explain, the waterfall calculation is paused and does not start until that difference is cleared.
How do you confirm the waterfall rules for the fund before calculating the distribution?

I work from the LPA, the side letters, the approved waterfall model, how it was treated before and the facts of the current event. I do this step together with the second reviewer and with input from the client.

I write down the exact order and definitions for return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest, the residual split and any holdback or clawback provision. I confirm whether the calculation applies to the whole fund, to each deal, to each tranche or to some other defined segment, and I confirm any escrow or holdback treatment. That is all recorded in the waterfall methodology record and the model.

The branch is whether the rules are clear. If the rule set is traceable to the governing documents and has been independently reviewed, I lock the rule set for this event and move on to running the cash waterfall. If a treatment has changed or a rule in the LPA is ambiguous, I record it, pause, and get written direction from the client or the legal adviser. We do not make up a missing rule ourselves. Once the written interpretation comes back, the rule set is locked and the work carries on.
How do you apply the locked rule set in the cash waterfall calculation?

I enter the current proceeds into the controlled model, which is the capital activity waterfall model, and apply the fund's return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in the approved order. From that I calculate the limited partner and general partner allocations, including any holdback.

Then I check it. Allocated cash plus retained or held cash has to equal the total modeled proceeds, and the result has to agree with the locked rules. What comes out is the draft cash waterfall result.

The branch in this step is the carry position. If the model shows the fund is in a carry position, the cash carry the waterfall allows is included in the result. If the fund is not in a carry position, no cash carry is paid. I document what the model shows and the reviewer confirms it. Either way I then move on to the tax side.

One more thing that can happen here: if the waterfall gives a negative, residual or otherwise unexpected result, I investigate it, and where the economics are unclear I get confirmation from the client or legal before going further.
What do you do first on the tax side after the cash waterfall result is ready?

The first thing is getting the taxable-income allocation for the event from the client's tax team or their tax adviser. They provide or approve the tax conclusions, and I only add them into the calculation. I confirm that the taxable income may differ from the cash, and I look at whether the GP or another investor is receiving taxable income without the corresponding cash.

That is where the branch is. If there is taxable income without cash carry, the client's tax adviser or the client decides whether a tax distribution is permitted or required. If the governing documents permit it, I calculate or add the tax distribution needed to cover the tax liability, in a dedicated section of the workbook, and I keep its support separate from the cash waterfall support. If it is not permitted, there is no tax distribution and I just carry the approved taxable-income allocation forward. Either way I get the tax team's or client's approval of the tax inputs and the output before I go on to withholding.

The other thing that can happen is that the required tax input is missing or conflicting. In that case the final economics are held until it is sorted out. We never replace the approved tax conclusion with one we worked out ourselves.
How do you determine and apply withholding once the tax inputs and output are approved?

I work from the client's or tax team's withholding schedule and their direction, in the capital activity workbook. I identify every investor who is subject to withholding and the jurisdiction and rate that applies to them. Then I either apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base, or I bring in the approved client schedule as it stands. Any approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments go in separately. For each investor I calculate the gross distribution, the withholding and the net cash.

The check is that gross minus withholding equals net cash for every investor, and that the schedule totals reconcile to the model and to the approved tax input. The second reviewer checks the result.

There are two branches in this step. The first is the type of event. If it is distribution-only, there is no netting and the net cash is simply gross less withholding. If it is a net event, I include the approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation, but I keep separate support for each component before netting, and the reviewer or the client confirms the netting.

The second is the schedule itself. If the withholding input is in and approved, I carry on to the investor allocations. If it is late or gets revised, or a rate, a jurisdiction or an investor classification is missing, I escalate to the client or the tax adviser, and the affected calculations, notices and payments are held or recalculated until we have the new version of the schedule and a renewed approval.
How do you turn the approved investor-level amounts into distribution notices?

Not straight away, there are a few steps before the notices. The amounts are not approved yet at this point. Notices are only produced after the internal review and after the client has approved the economics and we have locked the version. The step that comes right after withholding is applying the investor allocation rules, and that one is mine as the preparer.

I confirm the allocation basis the governing terms require, which can be the commitment percentage, the limited partner percentage, a deal-specific basis or another basis. I use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations. Then, in the allocation engine of the capital activity workbook, I calculate each investor's proceeds components, the carry and tax effects, the withholding and the net cash, and I reconcile the investor-level totals back to the fund-level waterfall and the tax schedules. Last, I populate the final summary tab, which is what the notices and the payment support are later built from. The result is the draft investor-level distribution schedule.

The branch is the reconciliation. If the investor totals equal the approved fund-level components, subject only to documented rounding, the package goes to the second reviewer for the internal review. If there is an allocation difference I cannot explain, or a percentage that is not supported by the governing method, I pause there until it is resolved. Percentages sitting in Excel are not treated as authoritative on their own.
What does the second reviewer check in the draft investor-level distribution schedule?

The second reviewer looks at more than the schedule. They get the whole package: the proceeds, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocation and notice-support working files, plus the draft notices.

They check the proceeds amount and classification and that the roll-forward is continuous from the prior event. They check the waterfall rules and formulas, the carried interest, the preferred return, the tax distribution and any holdback. They check the taxable-income and withholding inputs against the approved schedules. They check the investor totals, the gross, withholding and net calculations and the reconciliations. And on the draft notices they check the component labels, the GAAP and tax breakdowns and the footnotes. Their review comments are recorded and each one has to be resolved.

The branch is the outcome of that review. If everything is cleared, the second reviewer signs off, and that sign-off has to be in place before anything goes to the client. That gives us the internally cleared distribution package, and the next step is sending it to the client for approval. If there are unresolved errors or gaps in the source information, they come back to me as preparer, or go to the client or the tax adviser if it is their input, and the process stops there until they are fixed and the reviewer has cleared them.
After the internally cleared package is sent to the client, what happens before the economics are approved and the version is locked?

When I send the package I point out to the client every tax input that is still estimated, pending or late, so they know what might move. I coordinate this step and the client is the one who approves.

The branch is what the client comes back with. If they are happy with it as it stands, I get their final written approval, and then I lock and retain that version. The locked version is the one used for the notices, the posting and the payment. If they come back with changes, for example to timing, the character of the proceeds, tax amounts, withholding or the notice language, I incorporate the approved changes, recalculate the affected amounts, and repeat the reconciliations and the review checks. Then it goes back for the final written approval and I lock it. Nothing is released or paid from an unapproved version. The client's written approval has to be on file before any entry is recorded or any payment is made.

There are two exceptions around this step. If a change arrives after an entry has already been recorded or a payment made, we follow the controlled correction process and get renewed approval. And if a bank holiday or a cut-off time threatens the wires, the client and Treasury decide between changing the timing or agreeing an approved alternative execution plan, and we keep the revised calendar and the approval.
Once the version is locked, how are distribution notices produced?

They are produced from the locked approved investor schedule. I merge the investor data into the controlled Word notice template with a mail merge, and the notices come out as PDFs. Each notice discloses the gross proceeds, the components, the transaction type, taxable income, withholding, the net payment and any footnotes that apply. Then the second reviewer and I reconcile every notice back to the locked investor schedule and complete the QA.

In the same step I hand the approved posting and payment support over to the Fund Team and Treasury. From there it is executed through FA-01 and FA-17. Bank holidays and cut-off times are checked, the Fund Team records the general ledger entry, Treasury sends the wires, and Investor Services publishes the notices on the investor portal.

The branch is whether everything ties. If the notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all the FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete, the payment and the release go ahead. If there is a notice mismatch, a bank closure, invalid instructions or an incomplete approval, the payment or the release is held. Investor Services hold the release when a notice does not match the approved investor list, and Treasury holds payments when approvals, instructions or funding are incomplete or a holiday or cut-off gets in the way.
What confirms that the distribution is fully completed after the posting, wires and notice release?

There is one last step after the money goes out, and it is done by the assigned Fund Team or by me as the event preparer. I track the amounts withheld for tax separately from the investor net payments, and I give the supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority. I update the investor capital accounts and the historical contribution and distribution records, and I update the cumulative proceeds history and the carried-interest tracking. Then I reconcile the actual wires, the withholding held or remitted, the general ledger balances and the locked schedule. I also complete any client-specific uploads or open-template reporting. For One Rock, for example, the Cobalt upload has to be completed within two days of the event.

What confirms it is finished is that final reconciliation. Gross distribution has to equal net investor cash plus withholding, and the actual cash and the accounting have to agree to the locked event with no unexplained difference.

The branch is on that check. If it all reconciles, the event is closed out and we keep the reconciled post-distribution record and the remittance support. If there is unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference, I escalate it immediately and the closeout stays open. An unexplained difference prevents closeout and may need a correction or a reposting.

One thing I cannot tell you is who actually owns remitting the withholding to the tax authority. I do not know that, and I do not know the payment steps, the due dates or what counts as proof of remittance either. The tax process expert would be the person to confirm it. What I do know is that if the remittance owner is unclear on an event, the responsible role has to be assigned before closeout.
What are the practical consequences if a distribution is delayed or processed incorrectly?

steps.title: Provide written client classification

steps.title: Retain written confirmation
steps.description: Keep the client's written confirmation with the bank support.

steps.title: Model the event
steps.description: Modeling is reported as later work. In the escalated case, written client identification and classification are required first; modeling details and its other prerequisites are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Do proceeds and support reconcile?
steps.description: Check that total classified proceeds equal the amount being modeled and that every component has support. Bank activity alone may not establish the deal or character of the money.

steps.title: Obtain written client classification
steps.description: Stop calculations and obtain a written classification from the client when bank activity alone does not establish the deal or character of the money.

steps.title: Update cumulative proceeds
steps.description: Start with the prior approved cumulative proceeds working file and add current proceeds by supported classification.

steps.title: Confirm historical balances
steps.description: Confirm prior distributions, remaining invested capital and cumulative contributions.

steps.title: Reconcile cumulative balances
steps.system: System power report, trial balance and partner-capital files
steps.description: Reconcile starting and current balances to the prior event, general ledger, trial balance, bank records and partner-capital records. Pull the system power report, trial balance and partner-capital files for historical balances.

steps.title: Verify cumulative proceeds work
steps.description: Verify the preparer's cumulative proceeds and reconciliation work. The detailed review checks and timing relative to advancement are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Are reconciliation differences addressed?
steps.description: Determine whether every difference is resolved or documented, or whether the starting point has an unexplained difference.

steps.title: Wait for difference clearance
steps.description: Pause the waterfall calculation when a starting-point difference cannot be explained. The calculation cannot start until the difference is cleared.

steps.title: Confirm fund waterfall rules
steps.actor: Event preparer and second reviewer, with client input
steps.description: Use the LPA, side letters, approved model, prior treatment and current event facts to document the waterfall order and definitions. Confirm the calculation segment and escrow or holdback treatment.

steps.title: Are waterfall rules clear?
steps.description: Determine whether the rule set is traceable to governing documents and independently reviewed, or whether a changed treatment or ambiguous LPA rule requires written direction.

steps.title: Record issue and seek direction
steps.description: Record the changed treatment or ambiguous rule and seek written direction from the client or legal adviser. The work is paused; the team does not invent a missing rule.

steps.title: Wait for written interpretation
steps.description: Pause pending written interpretation from the client or legal adviser.

steps.title: Lock event rule set
steps.description: Lock the rule set for the event after the reported clear-rule checks or after written interpretation is received.

steps.title: Run cash waterfall
steps.description: Enter current proceeds into the controlled model and apply the fund's return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carried interest and residual calculations in the approved order. Calculate limited partner and general partner allocations, including any holdback.

steps.title: Check waterfall result
steps.description: Check that allocated cash plus retained or held cash equals total modeled proceeds and that the result agrees with the locked rules.

steps.title: Is the fund in carry?
steps.description: Determine the carry position shown by the model. Include the cash carry allowed by the waterfall if the fund is in carry; otherwise no cash carry is paid.

steps.title: Document carry position
steps.description: Document what the model shows about the carry position.

steps.title: Confirm carry position
steps.description: Confirm what the model shows about the carry position. Detailed checks and retained review evidence are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Investigate unexpected waterfall result
steps.description: Investigate a negative, residual or otherwise unexpected waterfall result. If the economics are unclear, obtain client or legal confirmation before going further.

steps.title: Obtain economics confirmation
steps.description: Obtain confirmation from the client or legal when the economics of an unexpected result are unclear, before going further.

steps.title: Obtain taxable-income allocation
steps.description: Obtain the event’s taxable-income allocation from the client’s tax team or tax adviser. They provide or approve the tax conclusions; the preparer does not substitute an independently determined conclusion.

steps.title: Add and assess tax allocation
steps.description: Add the tax conclusions into the calculation, confirm that taxable income may differ from cash, and look for taxable income allocated to the GP or another investor without corresponding cash.

steps.title: Is income without cash carry?
steps.description: Determine whether the reported taxable-income-without-cash-carry condition applies. The route when it does not apply is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Decide tax distribution treatment
steps.description: Decide whether a tax distribution is permitted or required when taxable income arises without cash carry. The participant refers to permission under the governing documents; who interprets them and how the decision is recorded are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate or add tax distribution
steps.description: Calculate or add the tax distribution needed to cover the tax liability in a dedicated workbook section. Keep its support separate from the cash waterfall support.

steps.title: Carry tax allocation forward
steps.description: If a tax distribution is not permitted, carry the approved taxable-income allocation forward without a tax distribution.

steps.title: Approve tax inputs and output
steps.description: Approve the tax inputs and output before withholding. The approval mechanism, retained evidence and rejection handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Identify withholding requirements
steps.description: Use the client’s or tax team’s withholding schedule and direction to identify each investor subject to withholding and the applicable jurisdiction and rate.

steps.title: Hold for tax input resolution
steps.description: Hold final economics when required tax input is missing or conflicting, until it is sorted out. The resolution process and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: How is withholding applied?
steps.description: Use either the approved rate and taxable-income base or the approved client schedule as supplied.

steps.title: Apply approved withholding rate
steps.description: Apply the approved rate to the approved taxable-income base.

steps.title: Bring in approved schedule
steps.description: Bring in the approved client withholding schedule as it stands. The transfer method is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate investor withholding amounts
steps.description: Include approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments separately. Calculate gross distribution, withholding and net cash for each investor.

steps.title: Do withholding amounts reconcile?
steps.description: Check that gross less withholding equals net cash for each investor and that schedule totals reconcile to the model and approved tax input.

steps.title: Review withholding result
steps.description: Check the withholding result. The reviewer’s specific checks, evidence and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is this a net event?
steps.description: Apply the event-type branch. Distribution-only events have no netting; net events include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation.

steps.title: Calculate net event
steps.description: Include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation and keep separate support for each component before netting.

steps.title: Confirm event netting
steps.description: Confirm the netting for a net event. The confirmation method and retained evidence are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is withholding input approved?
steps.description: Proceed to investor allocations when the withholding input is in and approved. Late or revised schedules and missing rates, jurisdictions or investor classifications require escalation and a hold or recalculation.

steps.title: Confirm investor allocation basis
steps.description: Confirm the basis required by the governing terms and use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations. The investor-level amounts are not yet approved.

steps.title: Escalate withholding input issues
steps.description: Escalate to the client or tax adviser when the schedule is late or revised, or a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing. Hold or recalculate affected calculations, notices and payments until the new schedule version and renewed approval are available.

steps.title: Wait for schedule and approval
steps.description: Affected calculations, notices and payments remain held or subject to recalculation until both the new schedule version and renewed approval are available. Their order and the exact resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate and reconcile allocations
steps.description: Calculate each investor's proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash. Reconcile investor totals to the fund-level waterfall and tax schedules.

steps.title: Populate final summary tab
steps.description: Populate the final summary tab from the investor allocation work. Notices and payment support are later built from it.

steps.title: Do investor allocations reconcile?
steps.description: Determine whether investor totals equal the approved fund-level components subject only to documented rounding. An unexplained difference or a percentage unsupported by the governing method pauses the work.

steps.title: Review and clear package
steps.system: Working files and draft notices; review-comment location UNKNOWN
steps.description: The second reviewer checks the proceeds, roll-forward, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocations and draft notices. Comments are recorded and must be resolved; errors return to the preparer, or client or tax adviser for their input, before reviewer clearance and sign-off.

steps.title: Wait for allocation resolution
steps.description: Pause when an allocation difference cannot be explained or a percentage is unsupported by the governing method. The resolution method and resumption point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Coordinate client approval
steps.description: The preparer sends the internally cleared package to the client, identifies estimated, pending or late tax inputs, and coordinates approval. If the client requests changes, the preparer incorporates approved changes, recalculates affected amounts and repeats reconciliations and review checks before seeking final written approval.

steps.title: Lock economics version
steps.description: After final written client approval, lock and retain the approved version for notices, posting and payment. A change after an entry or payment follows the controlled correction process and requires renewed approval; if a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, the client and Treasury decide timing or an approved alternative execution plan, and the revised calendar and approval are kept.

steps.title: Produce notices and close event
steps.actor: Event preparer, second reviewer, Fund Team, Treasury and Investor Services
steps.system: Capital activity workbook, controlled Word template, FA-01, FA-17, investor portal and Cobalt for One Rock
steps.description: The preparer produces PDF notices from the locked schedule; the preparer and second reviewer reconcile them and complete QA, and the preparer hands approved support to the Fund Team and Treasury. After payment, the assigned Fund Team or preparer updates records, supplies tax-payment support, completes applicable reporting and reconciles the event for closeout; exceptions are escalated and closeout remains open.

steps.description: Bring in the approved client withholding schedule as it stands. Transfer method is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate withholding amounts
steps.description: Include approved prior-period true-ups or supplemental adjustments separately. Calculate gross distribution, withholding and net cash for each investor.

steps.title: Do withholding amounts reconcile?
steps.description: Check gross less withholding equals net cash for each investor and schedule totals reconcile to the model and approved tax input.

steps.title: Review withholding result
steps.description: Check the withholding result. Specific checks, evidence and failure handling are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is this a net event?
steps.description: Distribution-only events have no netting; net events include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation.

steps.title: Calculate net event
steps.description: Include approved withholding in the call-and-distribution net calculation and keep separate support for each component before netting.

steps.title: Confirm event netting
steps.description: Confirm netting for a net event. Confirmation method and retained evidence are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Is withholding input approved?
steps.description: Proceed to investor allocations when withholding input is in and approved. Escalate late or revised schedules or missing rates, jurisdictions or investor classifications.

steps.title: Confirm allocation basis
steps.description: Confirm the basis required by governing terms: commitment percentage, limited partner percentage, deal-specific or another basis. Use the approved investor list and any approved special allocations. Investor-level amounts are not yet approved.

steps.title: Escalate withholding issues
steps.description: Escalate to the client or tax adviser if a schedule is late or revised, or a rate, jurisdiction or investor classification is missing. Hold or recalculate affected calculations, notices and payments until the new schedule version and renewed approval are available.

steps.title: Wait for schedule and approval
steps.description: Affected work remains held or subject to recalculation until both the new schedule version and renewed approval are available. Their order and the exact return point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Calculate and reconcile allocations
steps.description: Calculate each investor's proceeds components, carry and tax effects, withholding and net cash. Reconcile investor totals to the fund-level waterfall and tax schedules.

steps.title: Populate final summary tab
steps.description: Populate the final summary tab. Notices and payment support are later built from it.

steps.title: Do investor allocations reconcile?
steps.description: Determine whether investor totals equal approved fund-level components subject only to documented rounding. Pause for an unexplained allocation difference or a percentage unsupported by the governing method. Excel percentages alone are not authoritative.

steps.title: Review and clear package
steps.system: Working files and draft notices; comment location UNKNOWN
steps.description: Review the proceeds, waterfall, tax, withholding, allocation and notice-support files and draft notices. Check proceeds and classification, roll-forward continuity, rules and formulas, carry, preferred return, tax distribution and holdback; compare tax and withholding inputs with approved schedules; check investor totals, gross, withholding, net and reconciliations; and check notice labels, GAAP and tax breakdowns and footnotes. Record comments; each must be resolved. Sign off only when cleared, before anything goes to the client.

steps.title: Wait for allocation resolution
steps.description: Pause until an unexplained allocation difference or unsupported percentage is resolved. Resolution method and return point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Coordinate client approval
steps.description: Preparer sends the internally cleared package and points out tax inputs still estimated, pending or late. Client approves. If changes are requested, the preparer incorporates approved changes, recalculates affected amounts and repeats reconciliations and review checks before seeking final written approval.

steps.title: Lock economics version
steps.description: After final written client approval, lock and retain the version for notices, posting and payment. Nothing is released or paid from an unapproved version; written approval must be on file before an entry or payment.

steps.title: Produce approved notices
steps.description: Merge investor data from the locked approved schedule into the controlled Word template and produce PDFs. Notices disclose gross proceeds, components, transaction type, taxable income, withholding, net payment and applicable footnotes.

steps.title: Correct internal review issues
steps.actor: Event preparer, client or tax adviser as applicable
steps.description: Unresolved errors or source gaps return to the preparer, or to the client or tax adviser for their input. Work stops until fixed and the reviewer clears them.

steps.title: Reconcile notices and complete QA
steps.description: Reconcile every notice back to the locked investor schedule and complete QA.

steps.title: Hand over execution support
steps.description: Hand approved posting and payment support to the Fund Team and Treasury. Execution proceeds through FA-01 and FA-17; detailed gates and coordination are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Are release conditions met?
steps.description: Payment and release go ahead when notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete. Notice mismatch, bank closure, invalid instructions or incomplete approval can hold payment or release. Written client approval must be on file before entry or payment.

steps.title: Record general ledger entry
steps.description: Record the general ledger entry. Client written approval must be on file before any entry is recorded.

steps.title: Send investor wires
steps.description: Send wires when notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete. Written client approval must be on file before payment. Treasury holds payments for incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or a holiday or cut-off.

steps.title: Publish investor notices
steps.description: Publish notices when notice and payment totals agree to the locked schedule and all FA-01 and FA-17 gates are complete. Investor Services holds release when a notice does not match the approved investor list.

steps.title: Hold payment or release
steps.actor: Treasury or Investor Services, as applicable
steps.description: Hold the affected payment or release for a notice mismatch, bank closure, invalid instructions or incomplete approval. Investor Services holds mismatched notices; Treasury holds payments for incomplete approvals, instructions or funding, or a holiday or cut-off. Recovery is UNKNOWN except for the reported threatened-wire plan.

steps.title: Track withholding separately
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: After the money goes out, track amounts withheld for tax separately from investor net payments.

steps.title: Reconcile actual event
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Reconcile actual wires, withholding held or remitted, general ledger balances and locked schedule. Gross distribution must equal net investor cash plus withholding, and actual cash and accounting must agree to the locked event without unexplained difference.

steps.title: Close reconciled event
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Close out the reconciled event and keep the reconciled post-distribution record and remittance support. If remittance ownership is unclear, the responsible role must be assigned before closeout.

steps.title: Escalate closeout exception
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Immediately escalate unremitted withholding, a rejected wire or an accounting difference; keep closeout open. An unexplained difference prevents closeout and may need correction or reposting. Recipient and recovery route are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Assign remittance responsibility
steps.description: If the withholding remittance owner is unclear for an event, assign the responsible role before closeout. Who assigns it and how is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Follow controlled correction process
steps.description: If a change arrives after an entry has been recorded or payment made, follow the controlled correction process and obtain renewed approval. Internal actions and return point are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Decide threatened-wire plan
steps.description: If a bank holiday or cut-off threatens wires, decide between changing timing and agreeing an approved alternative execution plan. Keep the revised calendar and approval.

steps.title: Provide tax-payment support
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Give supporting records to whoever is responsible for paying the tax authority. The participant does not know the remittance owner, payment steps, due dates or proof requirements; the tax process expert can confirm them.

steps.title: Complete applicable client reporting
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.system: Cobalt for One Rock; other systems UNKNOWN
steps.description: Complete applicable client-specific uploads or open-template reporting. For One Rock, complete the Cobalt upload within two days of the event. Other applicable clients, insertion and return points are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Update distribution histories
steps.actor: Assigned Fund Team or event preparer
steps.description: Update investor capital accounts, historical contribution and distribution records, cumulative proceeds history and carried-interest tracking.

topics.answer: The intake calls this Distribution Economics: Waterfall, Tax Withholding & Notices. It covers event setup through distribution closeout in the participant's account. Other team or checklist names and the parent boundary are UNKNOWN.

The work produces approved distribution economics, investor notices and execution support, and a reconciled post-distribution record. The participant did not separately state the full recipient value or downstream boundary.

Received or expected proceeds, a deal closing or realization, or a client request starts the event-driven work; there is no fixed calendar. The preparer confirms the requested payment date. Detection and notification are UNKNOWN; One Rock reporting has a separate two-day deadline.

Closeout follows final reconciliation: gross equals net investor cash plus withholding, and actual cash and accounting agree to the locked event without unexplained differences. The reconciled record and remittance support are retained, and an unclear remittance role must be assigned. Remittance proof, evidence location and downstream consumer are UNKNOWN.

UNKNOWN: the overall accountable role was not identified. The event preparer coordinates work, the client approves economics, and the assigned Fund Team or preparer performs closeout; these duties do not establish overall accountability.

The preparer briefs the event, classifies proceeds, rolls forward and reconciles history, confirms and locks rules, runs the waterfall, adds client-approved tax conclusions, applies withholding and calculates investor allocations. A second reviewer clears the package; the client approves and the preparer locks it. Notices and execution support follow, then post-payment records and reconciliation. Client classification, rule interpretation, tax inputs, review corrections and execution holds can interrupt this route; several returns and the draft-notice preparation point are UNKNOWN.

Reported checks cover supported proceeds, reconciled historical balances, traceable and reviewed waterfall rules, cash tie-outs, approved tax inputs, investor withholding and allocation reconciliations, detailed second review, client written approval, notice QA, execution gates and final reconciliation. Review comments must be resolved; client changes are recalculated and re-reviewed. Evidence locations, some failure handling, thresholds, segregation and system enforcement remain UNKNOWN.

Distribution-only events do not net; net events include withholding in a supported call-and-distribution calculation confirmed by a reviewer or client. Tax distributions depend on the client or adviser decision and reported governing-document permission. One Rock has a Cobalt upload within two days. Reasons, effort, charging, removability and boundary tests are UNKNOWN.
